observed_problem: The Core v2 release workflow publishes the irreversible GitHub Release before adopting the FROZEN stage and committing RELEASED provenance. If a later adoption or provenance-PR step fails, the public Release exists while canonical main remains FROZEN, and a rerun fails immediately because the release tag already exists.
expected_behavior: The external Release boundary must have explicit reconciliation/idempotency authority. A retry after a partial external success must verify the existing issue-only Release and exact PDF bytes, then complete the missing State/Release Record provenance without silently replacing or duplicating public bytes.
actual_behavior: stage:release is declared non-retryable and the workflow rejects any pre-existing release tag. There is therefore no supported recovery path for a public-success/provenance-failure split brain.
production_workaround: External W33/SP001 production remains blocked until the coherent Core v2 candidate is Human-reviewed and merged; exact-byte release reconciliation is implemented and regression-covered on this branch.
improvement_action: Give stage:release explicit external-key idempotency/reconciliation authority and make the release workflow accept an existing release only after fail-closed verification of tag/title/target and the exact frozen PDF asset SHA/size; then continue missing provenance adoption.
